summary: Initial discovery for Summit Telecom's interest in a Redwood Private VPC deployment. Main topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, cross-account peering, transit gateway, region constraints (APAC/NA), restrictions around egress via NAT, KMS/HSM key management, SSO/SAML and audit log access. Redwood AE/SE outlined deployment options, networking requirements, and next steps to run a performance benchmark and share security docs. Customer requested a technical deep dive focusing on network setup and a timeline for a pilot.
topics: deployment models: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Carlos (CTO, Summit Telecom), Priya (Head Infra), Mark (Security), Elena (Cloud Architect)

00:00 - Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samira from Redwood Inference, i'm with Jon our SE. quick agenda, understand your network constraints for a Private VPC deployment and see if dedicated/reserved vs private makes sense.
00:12 - Carlos: yeah thanks, we are on a tight timeline, trying to get a pilot running in september, primary blockers are networking and compliance.
00:20 - Jon: great; can you describe current cloud layout, regions, transit?
00:30 - Priya: so majority of infra is in us-east-1 and ap-southeast-1, we use a transit gateway for most inter-VPC traffic, we also have a colo in la for some low-latency stuff. we prefer no public egress for inference traffic, so private endpoints or peering only.
00:45 - Mark: and from security side, we need KMS integration (customer-managed keys/HSM), SOC2 evidence, audit logs for every inference request, and SSO via SAML. also data residency is a thing for telco CDRs, need to keep certain tokens in-region.
01:02 - Jon: ok that fits our Private offering; we support VPC peering, transit-gw peering, and AWS PrivateLink style private endpoints depending on model. note, egress restrictions and cross-region come with tradeoffs - peering is simplest intra-region but not cross-region without transit.
01:20 - Priya: clarifying - you support cross-account peering? our infra team wants Redwood to deploy into our account, or we can run a customer-managed deployment; what's typical?
01:30 - Samira: most customers do a private deployment with Redwood control plane in our managed plane but the inference nodes in the customer's VPC via a deployment bundle; alternatives are dedicated (Redwood-owned VPC with peering) or hosted (public endpoints, not acceptable here). cross-account role + stack deploy is common - it allows us to create resources in your account with least-priv perms.
01:48 - Carlos: can you do cross-region? our APAC region is strict, we need inference to stay in ap-southeast-1 for latency and regulation.
01:56 - Jon: yes, we can provision inference pools in specific regions. two things: model versions and weights need to be present in-region, and if you want active-active across regions we need a replication strategy for KV cache and model artifacts; that can add cost/complexity.
02:20 - Mark: about private endpoints - do you use AWS NLB + PrivateLink, or do you rely on peering? what about mutual TLS?
02:29 - Jon: we typically offer two patterns: 1) VPC peering/transit gateway where we've got ENIs in your VPC and traffic stays within, or 2) AWS PrivateLink/NLB to expose a private endpoint into your VPC. PrivateLink gives more security isolation and is easier for cross-account without peering. mTLS is supported between nodes and we can validate with customer CA if needed.
02:50 - Priya: our network team is worried about route table complexity and overlapping CIDRs, we use 10.0.0.0/16 in many VPCs. can you accommodate custom CIDR ranges?
03:00 - Jon: yes, we do support configuring resources to avoid collisions; there are known constraints with peering and overlapping CIDRs - PrivateLink avoids that. we normally ask for your CIDR ranges and propose subnets for our ENIs.
03:18 - Carlos: what's the latency profile? we can't have >50ms p95 for certain features. how does Redwood measure latency and what are realistic expectations if the inference cluster is in our VPC?
03:28 - Jon: good question; latency depends on model size, quantization, and network hop. with an in-VPC deployment with ENIs, p95 token latency for small models is typically low single-digit ms for inference compute plus network hop; for large LLMs expect tens of ms. our Optimize tooling can reduce cost/latency via batching and KV cache, but we'll want to run a benchmark with your payloads.
04:00 - Elena: about bandwidth - we have heavy embedding workloads outbound to our analytics cluster, will Redwood support egress controls and VPC endpoints to keep traffic internal?
04:10 - Samira: yes you can configure egress rules; for some customers we set up routing through private peering to internal analytics VPCs. we'll also document the required security groups, subnets, and NAT needs if model artifacts need to be pulled from S3 (you can allow S3 private endpoints).
04:35 - Mark: audit logs - we need per-request metadata for compliance, retention 7 years. can you stream logs to our SIEM or S3?
04:44 - Jon: we can forward structured audit logs to customer endpoints (S3, Kinesis, or a SIEM) and configure retention. we do include token-level cost/latency metrics - note PII will be redacted unless you want verbosity. we'll surface an audit schema.
05:05 - Priya: ok quick question on keys - we want CMEK in our account; can Redwood use customer-managed KMS keys?
05:13 - Jon: yes, we support customer KMS; for HSM-backed keys we'd coordinate key policies for the service principal. we can also do envelope encryption on top.
05:25 - Carlos: is there a managed control plane that still calls home? is that a dealbreaker? we need the control plane to be able to orchestrate but cannot have our data plane egress.
05:35 - Samira: control plane traffic is minimal; common pattern is control plane in Redwood account for billing/rollouts, with data plane entirely in-customer VPC. we can sign an SLA and do isolated control plane peering if needed.
05:50 - Elena: timeline - what would a pilot look like? two-week perf run?
05:56 - Jon: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: initial infra provisioning and network validation (1 week), load & perf benchmark with sample prompts (1-2 weeks), then post-mortem and recommendation. we'll need your CIDRs and sandbox data.
06:10 - Mark: any red flags around compliance with telco data - e.g., full call detail records?
06:18 - Samira: we'd recommend running sensitive data through a redaction/pseudonymization step before sending to the model, but we support in-region deployments and strict audit logging. we'll share our compliance pack and patterns.
06:35 - Carlos: competitors - we evaluated MegaInference and VendorX; what differentiates Redwood here?
06:42 - Samira: Ops & network flexibility; our runtime can live in-customer VPC with full observability and cost controls. VendorX required opening public endpoints or heavy VPNs. MegaInference has good speed but limited private deployment tooling.
07:00 - Priya: ok, let's talk technical constraints: do you need open internet access for nodes to pull images, model weights, or is a VPC with S3 VPC endpoints sufficient?
07:12 - Jon: S3 VPC endpoints plus ECR private access or pre-baked AMIs is sufficient. if you have a locked-down environment we can arrange an offline artifact sync or pull via a customer-managed bastion.
07:30 - Elena: cross-region traffic - we want to avoid cross-region data transfer for regulatory reasons. can we pin inference to ap-southeast-1 only?
07:40 - Jon: yes, you can pin. if you later want DR in us-east-1 we can do async replication but you control where weights live.
07:55 - Carlos: any IAM patterns you recommend?
08:00 - Jon: we usually provide a CloudFormation/ARM/Terraform template that creates a least-priv service role, ENIs, and security groups. we also support cross-account IAM roles for control plane to assume when performing ops. we'll share templates.
08:20 - Mark: monitoring - can we get per-request traces into our X-Ray/Jaeger setup?
08:28 - Jon: we can emit traces; we have tracing hooks that forward to customer collectors, or we can send a copy to Redwood for dashboarding.
08:40 - Samira: ok wrapping - sounds like main blockers are (1) we need CIDR ranges and confirmation of which accounts to deploy into, (2) security pack review, (3) schedule deep-dive and perf window. any other asks?
08:55 - Priya: can you send an example network diagram and the exact ports/protocols needed?
09:02 - Jon: yes, i'll attach a network guide showing ports (ENI - TCP 443, control plane 443 outbound to control plane IPs, optional port for mTLS) and sample diagrams for peering vs privatelink.
09:20 - Carlos: budget - is private deployment substantially more expensive than dedicated?
09:26 - Samira: private tends to be higher upfront ops but lower long-term due to data egress savings and self-managed infra; dedicated is Redwood-owned infra with peering and predictable throughput, sometimes cheaper short-term. we'll provide SKU examples.
09:45 - Mark: ok next steps: send security docs, network diagram, schedule SE deep dive.
09:52 - Samira: perfect, we'll follow up with an email and set up the deep dive. thanks everyone.
10:00 - [call ended]
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors and speaker attribution approximations; call was AE+SE led with clear ask for technical deep dive and pilot. Customer emphasized in-region constraints and strict audit/logging needs.
